messages:
Priya Singh: FYI FinLedger wants a firm committed plan + simple procurement numbers. They specified ~120 RPS steady, short peaks to ~600 RPS, 3 AZs, CMK for encryption, and a 12mo reserve. Need: recommended reserved GPU count, burst strategy, and a compact cost appendix for legal. Meeting with procurement Tue 9am PT.

Jamal Rivera: Can we confirm token mix? avg request tokens and response tokens? and are they okay with occasional degraded quality to meet latency?

Priya Singh: Customer replied: request payloads small, avg response ~110 tokens, ~7% sessions go long (~1k tokens). They prefer no visible quality degradation but accept short fallback windows.

Marco Chen: Quick capacity math: conservative per-GPU throughput for LLM-70B quant (4-bit) on our runtime: ~9 RPS for 100-150 token responses at low batching, ~13 RPS with KV cache + decent batching. For steady 120 RPS baseline -> 120/11 = 10.9 RPS per GPU -> I'd pick 11 GPUs reserved to hit ~70% util, leaving headroom.

Marco Chen: Spike handling: prewarmed burst pool sized for ~40% of spike (i.e., ~192 RPS worth), plus autoscale into on-demand up to 6x the reserve. Recommend a short warm-up of 90-120s for nodes and keep some standing burst capacity.

Elena Ortiz: Proposed autoscale params (POC draft):
```
target_util_pct: 70
prewarm_pct: 40
burst_reserved_pct: 20
max_scale_multiplier: 6
burst_cooldown_sec: 90
```
This biases toward faster response during short spikes at cost of extra reserved prewarm.

Priya Singh: Procurement wants monthly committed number + a simple hourly burst rate example for 2-hour spike. Jamal can you draft the example table?

Jamal Rivera: I'll make a short table: 8/10/11/14 GPUs -> expected p95 latency and monthly committed cost. Need Marco's microbench numbers to fill latencies.

Marco Chen: I'll run a 1hr perfbench on staging today for 8/10/11/14 GPUs and post p95/mean CPU/GPU util and tail latencies. I'll include a 2-hour simulated spike test to show graceful degradation.

ops-bot: autoscale-policy "finledger-commit-v2" created in staging (policy-id: sp-4421).

Elena Ortiz: Draft runbook bullets for deck:
- Reserved: 11 GPUs across 3 AZs (spread evenly, 4/4/3).
- Prewarm: 40% during business hours, lower at night (schedule attached).
- Burst: combine reserved prewarm + on-demand autoscale with max multiplier 6 and a fallback to smaller model at p95>600ms.
- Security: CMK rotation supported; we need their KMS ARN to confirm access.

Priya Singh: Action items: Marco -> bench + table; Elena -> pricing appendix + runbook doc; Jamal -> procurement table wording; I'll send calendar invite for Tue 9am PT.

Marco Chen: Bench started. ETA 6 hours. Will post results in this thread and upload artifacts to /deals/FinLedger/bench-results/.

Priya Singh: Great — please ping when results are up. Also capture cost delta between 11 and 14 GPUs so procurement can see marginal benefit.

Elena Ortiz: Placed a placeholder slide in the shared deal deck: /deals/FinLedger/commit-pricing-appendix.pptx — will update after Marco posts numbers.

Jamal Rivera: I'll join Tue call for the technical Qs.

Priya Singh: Thanks team. Reminder: keep the numbers labeled "indicative" until legal approves final pricing.
